memory_lessons.applicability: Use these aggregate results as a warning against assuming a direct small-input path wins; they do not show per-size effects or causes.
memory_lessons.claim: Both measured direct candidates were valid but had slightly higher complete-run means than baseline: 47.0667 μs for the 512-bound shared-memory variant and 46.9589 μs for the 2048-bound warp-shuffle variant, compared with 46.7866 μs baseline.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare a single-warp direct reduction with no shared-memory block reduction against the staged path, preserving n=1 as a copy-only control.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured 512-element shared-memory direct path (9398cac053fc446f: 47.0667 μs) and the 2048-element warp-shuffle path (5c526c5e47cb4297: 46.9589 μs) were both correct but slightly slower in complete-run aggregates than the 46.7866 μs baseline. Those aggregates do not isolate small-n behavior. Test a structurally different one-warp reduction for 2 <= n <= 128: 32 lanes accumulate at most four values each and use the existing warp reduction helper to write directly to out, avoiding shared memory and block barriers. Keep n=1 copy-only and n>128 staged. The 128 bound follows four values per lane, not a benchmark-size specialization; complete-run performance remains unmeasured.

retained: Replace the parent 128-thread shared-memory small-input kernel with a single-warp direct kernel using the existing warpReduceSum helper.
Dispatch 2 <= n <= 128 to the one-warp kernel, a generic bound of four input values per lane; retain n=1 device-copy behavior and use the existing staged path for larger sizes.
